subject: Pilot acceptance gates and evaluation checklist
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire@clearviewhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot acceptance gates and evaluation checklist

Hi Claire —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a first-pass MAP + evaluation checklist for the ClearView pilot. High level:

- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for clinical summarization use case across 1M tokens of synthetic traffic and 3 real-user workflows.
- Duration: 3 week technical pilot + 2 week ops stabilization.
- Key acceptance gates (proposed): smoke pass, quality threshold (ROUGE-L / task-specific), infra SLOs, compliance evidence.

Action items I need from your side to lock the MAP:
1) Confirm which workflows we should seed with real user data (A, B or A+B).
2) Procurement contact for PO / SSO requirements.
3) Any non-functional gating bars beyond latency and availability (e.g., PII redaction).

I've attached the spreadsheet "redwood_eval_checklist.xlsx" with a proposed break-down: test owner, acceptance metric, pass threshold, and rollback trigger. Ben is cc'd to add SE-level pass/fail tests.

Can we target a short sync on Friday to finalize? If you prefer, we can convert the checklist into a mutual action plan doc and share a canary deployment schedule.

Best,
Monica
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Adding some SE detail on acceptance tests and rollback criteria so the MAP can be operationalized. High-level technical pass/fail candidates:

1) Smoke tests (run after canary deploy, owner: SE)
   - End-to-end inference for 10 representative transcripts succeeds within 95% (no runtime exceptions).
   - Basic semantic checks: output not empty, not a fixed token repeat.

2) Latency / throughput (owner: Infra/SE)
   - P95 latency < 450ms for 1k token median prompt (with requested batching config).
   - Sustained QPS >= 150 for the pilot workload.

3) Quality checks (owner: Data/Customer)
   - On the agreed 20-prompt rubric: mean acceptability >= 0.80 (manual triage score).
   - Task-specific metric: entity extraction F1 >= 0.87 on the provided sample set.

4) Regression signals (owner: Redwood QA)
   - No increase >2% in hallucination incidents against baseline.

5) Rollback triggers (owner: Eng/SE)
   - Any two-severity production errors in 24 hours, or P95 > 750ms for more than 30 minutes -> rollback to previous model variant.

I've also attached "se_runbook.md" with test commands, endpoints, and suggested canary windows. Happy to walk through on Friday and map owners to each checklist row.

- Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 08:45:00 -0700

Thanks both — based on Ben's SE bullets I've updated the MAP spreadsheet with a task tracker and an explicit canary schedule:

Week 0 (pre-work): SSO + provisioning, sampling & prompt-set exchange, access and logging config.
Week 1 (canary): 10% of traffic to canary for 48 hours. Smoke tests run at T+2h, full smoke suite at T+24h.
Week 2 (ramp): 50% traffic for 72 hours, run full evaluation on the 20-prompt set; QA to surface hallucination incidents.
Week 3 (verification): 100% traffic, run regression checks and final signoff.

Acceptance gate matrix (summary):
- Gate 1: Canary smoke pass -> requires green on smoke + no critical errors.
- Gate 2: Quality gate -> manual acceptability >= 0.80 on sample set + entity F1 >= 0.87.
- Gate 3: Ops gate -> P95 <= 450ms and error rate < 0.5%.

Rollback ladder (examples):
- Immediate rollback: critical data leak, P95 > 750ms for 30m, or >5% of responses fail safety checks.
- Graceful rollback: significant quality regression flagged by manual triage (>5 examples).

I also added owners and estimated SLAs to each line in the spreadsheet. Can we confirm SOC2 note and SSO items (Claire)? Once procurement confirms PO timing we will publish the MAP and schedule DocuSign.

Thanks,
Monica
